title: Edge egress fragmentation and DNS truncation notes
body:
Summary:
Observed intermittent TLS handshake failures from customer private deployments to external SaaS endpoints when responses were large (DNS + HTTP). Hypothesis: large UDP DNS responses are being truncated or fragmented across an overlay path with a reduced MTU; fallback to TCP then encounters path MTU issues / MSS clamping problems causing stalls and TLS resets.

Context and why this is weird:
- Only affects private deployments that peer through our edge transit path (partner transit + GW tunnel). Hosted API unaffected.
- Failures correlate with queries that return large EDNS0/RRSIG/DNSSEC responses and with egress flows that include TCP handshakes immediately after DNS.
- Symptoms: long pauses during TLS handshake (client hello sent, server hello delayed or never seen), followed by TCP retransmits then RSTs.

Timeline (quick):
- 2025-02-12: customer reports timeouts during auth to external provider (OAuth), intermittent.
- 2025-02-13: initial capture shows DNS responses with TC bit set sometimes; for the same query other networks return full UDP answer.
- 2025-02-14: reproduced in lab by forcing large DNS response via test DNS server with EDNS0.
- 2025-02-15: ran path MTU/df tests and saw ICMP "fragmentation needed" from partner peer.

Commands / captures (useful snippets):
- dig using UDP (shows TC sometimes):
  dig +noall +answer @10.1.2.3 large.example.com +edns=0 +bufsize=4096
  ;; -> response shows flags: -> | tc | sometimes present

- force TCP DNS and compare:
  dig +tcp @10.1.2.3 large.example.com
  ;; TCP returns full answer reliably (in lab)

- tcpdump around time of TLS stall:
  07:12:34.567891 IP 10.20.30.5.54321 > 54.23.12.8.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 12345 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
  07:12:34.678901 IP 54.23.12.8.443 > 10.20.30.5.54321: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 28960, options [mss 1460], length 0
  07:12:34.679101 IP 10.20.30.5.54321 > 54.23.12.8.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:501, ack 1, win 64240, length 500
  [no server response for ~3s] then retransmits and a subsequent RST from server side

- tracepath / trace (shows MTU blackhole):
  tracepath 54.23.12.8
  1?: 10.0.0.1                                         0.123ms pmtu 1400
  2: 100.64.0.1                                        1.234ms
  pmtu 1400
  (we see pmtu dropped to 1400 on the tunnel)

- ping with DF set to trigger ICMP frag-needed:
  ping -M do -s 1400 54.23.12.8
  From 100.64.0.1 icmp_seq=1 Frag needed and DF set (mtu = 1400)

- kernel dmesg / icmp logs on edge: show "ip: local error - returned ICMP frag needed" in some captures.

What we tried and results:
- Set DNS forwarder to prefer TCP for specific large zones: fixes the DNS truncation but not the subsequent TCP stall (still see long stalls).
- Enabled iptables MSS clamp (clamp to pmtu) on the egress NAT box: seemed to reduce stalls significantly in lab.
- Increased MTU on tunnel interface to 1420 for test lane: transient improvement but partner peer rejected >1400 (so not a long term fix).
- Forced TCP for DNS + reduced EDNS buffer size (4096 -> 1232): reduces occurrences but not ideal.
- Temporarily route problematic customer via alternative transit (direct cloud peer) -> success (no stalls).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Primary: overlay/tunnel pmtu (1400) + large UDP DNS responses cause fragmentation/truncation. When client retries over TCP, sequence path experiences MSS/PMTU mismatch (e.g., no MSS clamping on NAT hop or intermediate load balancer) so TCP segments containing TLS handshake get dropped/fragmented resulting in handshake timeouts.
2) Secondary: conntrack table entry / NAT mapping for initial UDP query changes state such that immediate TCP coming from same client uses a different 5-tuple (src port changed) and hits a different SNAT path with worse MTU; less likely but possible with port-preserving weirdness.
3) Tertiary: middlebox (partner) inspects large UDP and deliberately truncates / rate-limits UDP large responses to force TCP which is then deprioritized by their transit queueing causing timeouts.

Repro recipe (lab):
1) Launch a VM connected through the same type of tunnel (vlan/gre/vxlan) with pmtu 1400 enforced.
2) Run a test authoritative DNS server that answers with a 1400+ UDP response (EDNS0 + DNSSEC or large TXT).
3) From test client, resolve and then immediately open TLS connection to a test server behind same egress path (simulate the OAuth exchange).
4) Capture tcpdump on egress node and at partner edge.

Quick mitigations (short-term):
- Enable MSS clamping on NAT egress (iptables --clamp-mss-to-pmtu). Rollout to affected customer instances only. Needs QA.
- Configure authoritative/internal resolvers to prefer TCP for known large-authority zones or reduce EDNS0 buffer size to 1232 on forwarders.
- Provide customer with routing alternative (direct peer) while we work the long-term fix.

Longer-term fixes to evaluate:
- Automate detection of large DNS UDP responses and translate to TCP proxied responses (transparent proxy) at edge.
- Work with partner transit to raise MTU or to ensure MSS clamp behavior end-to-end.
- Add observability: per-request DNS response size histogram; correlate with subsequent TCP handshake latencies.
- Improve our default forwarder to fall back to TCP faster (detect truncation and proactively open TCP prefetch for candidate flows).

Open action items:
- [Priya] Draft quick rollout plan for MSS clamp on affected egress NATs; test and stage to two canaries (ETA 2d).
- [Ethan] Add an ad-hoc datapoint in tracing pipeline to attach previous DNS response size for TLS connection events (small POC) (ETA 1w).
- [Luis] Open partner ticket to confirm tunnel MTU and whether they can support 1420 or run MSS clamp on their egressers (ETA 3d).
- [Priya/Ethan] Add a synthetic monitor that issues a large-EDNS query then establishes TLS to an external host and records handshake time (ETA 1w).

Notes / things to check later:
- Verify conntrack timeouts and port preservation behavior across the NAT box when UDP->TCP flows happen quickly.
- Check for any load-balancer TCP segmentation offload (TSO/GSO) interactions that could produce large on-wire segments unexpectedly.
- Audit iptables/nft rules history around the time customer incidents started (did a deploy remove MSS clamp?).

Random logs / snippets saved (raw):
- ICMP frag-needed seen: "From 100.64.0.1: ICMP Frag needed and DF set (mtu=1400)"
- DNS tcp fallback hit: "resolver: query truncated, reconnecting via tcp"
- Client side timeline (short): DNS query 07:12:34.500 -> DNS answer truncated -> client issues TCP fallback (short) -> TCP SYN 07:12:34.567 -> SYN/ACK -> client sends long TLS ClientHello 500 bytes -> server silence -> retransmit -> reset.

Brain dump / longer thoughts (freeform):
- This is the kind of problem that's easy to misattribute to 'the internet' — need to show reproducible pattern and clear before/after for MSS clamp to convince partner/ops.
- We should not disable EDNS0 globally; better to scope solutions to problematic zones and egress paths.
- Consider adding a proactive 'fail fast to TCP' policy for resolvers used on private deployments: if EDNS0 answer > 1000 bytes, try TCP first for subsequent queries to same authority.

If you pick this up: start by repro in lab following the recipe above and confirm that iptables --clamp-mss-to-pmtu on the NAT node removes the delay. If true, run canary rollouts + metrics (TLS handshake latency) before broad rollout.

----
Notes-to-self: keep captures in /tmp/egress-captures/edge-frag-2025-02-14.tar.gz and attach to INC-4521.
